summary: A settled signature verdict no longer keeps a judging row, and the rows earlier releases kept are deleted in short paced pages after upgrade. Saved idempotency responses now last 24 hours instead of 7 days, and the receipts from before 2026-10-07, which were kept for a deployment+30d follow-up, now expire. The hourly retention pass gives the freed pages back. Measured on a copy of a real member, this gave back 9.0% of the file: about 1.5 KB per signed claim from the judging rows, plus about 4.4 KB per saved response older than a day. A typical member frees about that much. Free pages now go back 128 per write instead of 512, which keeps each write under 100 ms.

replay.detail: No graph replay and no history scan at open. The prune walks claim_signature_judging in claim order from a cursor in meta, 512 rows or 10 ms per writer loan with an equal quiet interval after each, once the signature migration is done; response expiry keeps its 64-row, 20 ms chunks.

schema.detail: One trigger is added, claim_verdict_queue_marks_pruned: when a claim with no judging row is queued for judgment again, it gets a dirty placeholder row, so it reads as pending until rejudged, as a dirty row made it read before. The idempotency_completed_expiry trigger is recreated once with the 24-hour window. Two meta keys are added: claim_signature_judging_prune (the prune cursor) and idempotency_retention_24h_rowid (the last receipt written under the 7-day window). No table, column, index, kind, digest or storage version changes; storage stays at 20.

rules.detail: Verdicts, signatures, nonces, candidates, the served per-claim signature (claim_signatures), dependency links and their requeue are unchanged. A row is deleted only when its fold is complete, clean, unblocked and notified, with at most 32 candidates matching claim_signature_counts: such a claim is judged directly from its candidates and never reads the row. Claims with more than 32 candidates keep their completed result witness. A saved response is still kept while its runtime generation uses it; after expiry a retry gets idempotency-key-expired with the original claim id, as after 7 days before.

compatibility.detail: No synced table or digest changes, so peers of any version are unaffected in both directions (measured: replication inventory digest equal before and after the prune). The previous release reads a missing judging row as never paged: verdict reads see nothing pending, and its next judgment of the claim inserts a fresh row. It keeps the new queue trigger, which it does not know, so a revocation, nonce or root requeue it runs after a rollback still marks pruned claims pending. It keeps the 24-hour expiry trigger and honours each receipt's stored expiry.

downtime.detail: No downtime. Measured on a copy of the member: longest prune loan 50 ms (p99 32 ms), longest response-expiry loan 55 ms (p99 38 ms), longest free-page write 79 ms (p99 53 ms) at 128 pages per write; at the earlier 512 pages it reached 225 ms. The prune finished in about 6,300 loans, and the free pages went back in about 10,400 writes, 50 ms apart.

manual.detail: Nothing to do on a store with incremental auto-vacuum (PRAGMA auto_vacuum answers 2, as every store created from 2026-10-18 on does). A store created before then reuses the freed pages for new data but its file does not shrink. Convert it once with the daemon stopped, with free disk as large as the store, using the command in docs/st3/retention.md: python3 -c 'import sqlite3, sys; c = sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1]); c.execute("PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL"); c.execute("VACUUM")' "$STATE/claims.sqlite3". It cannot be paced: a VACUUM rewrites the whole file in one write, so the daemon cannot run it.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported. Deleted judging rows are resume state only: they are recomputed from the retained candidates whenever a claim is judged again. Expired responses cannot be restored; their claims still identify the operation.
